items.headline: Exports top US$15 billion
items.summary: Sri Lanka's goods and services exports passed US$15.28 billion in January–October, a record pace, the Export Development Board said. Electronics, food, spices and ICT led growth, while apparel and tea were weaker.

items.headline: Court keeps Gotabaya travel ban
items.summary: The Colombo Fort Magistrate's Court refused to temporarily lift former President Gotabaya Rajapaksa's overseas travel ban in the Easter attacks probe. It told the CID to clarify urgently whether he will be named a suspect; his appeal against a possible PTA arrest will be heard in March.

items.headline: Inflation rises to 8.5% in October
items.summary: National consumer price inflation climbed to 8.5% in October from 8.1%, the highest this year. Petrol, bus fares and other transport costs were the biggest contributors, with food inflation up to 7.2%.

items.headline: Sri Lanka women win Emerging Nations Trophy
items.summary: Sri Lanka bowled Ireland out for 96 in the final to win the ICC Women's Emerging Nations Trophy.

items.headline: Road cave-in snarls traffic at Liberty
items.summary: Part of Duplication Road in Kollupitiya collapsed near Liberty Roundabout, cutting traffic to one lane. Police advised motorists to use other routes.

items.headline: Fisheries talks with India in January
items.summary: Fisheries Minister Ramalingam Chandrasekar said a joint working group will meet in New Delhi on 22 January to seek a lasting fix for Indian trawlers fishing in Sri Lankan waters.

items.headline: Ethics framework to curb misleading ads
items.summary: The government plans a social ethics framework to address discriminatory and misleading advertising. Separately, a minister's office denied reports of a ban on caste references in matrimonial ads.

items.headline: Govt pledges equal healthcare access
items.summary: The government said it is committed to giving all citizens equal access to quality healthcare.

items.headline: Kurunegala–Galewela expressway work to start
items.summary: Construction of the Kurunegala–Galewela expressway section is due to begin on 1 December. Access Engineering won the largest share of Rs. 68 bn in Ruwanpura Expressway contracts.

items.headline: Disabled cargo ship towed to Hambantota
items.summary: Hambantota Port berthed the Cyprus-flagged MV AAL Gibraltar, which lost propulsion after engine-room flooding, for repairs.

items.headline: No bail in Kavantissa tusker shooting
items.summary: A Mahawa court remanded two suspects in the shooting of the tusker Kavantissa until 9 December and asked the Wildlife Department for a valuation of the elephant and the final post-mortem report.

items.headline: Arrest warrant for Rajangane Saddharathana
items.summary: The Colombo Fort court issued a warrant after he failed to appear in a case over social media remarks said to threaten religious harmony.

items.headline: Ananda Palitha further remanded
items.summary: SJB executive member Ananda Palitha was further remanded over an alleged Rs. 3.1 mn overtime fraud at the CPC.

items.headline: Mother and son slashed in Kolonnawa
items.summary: A mother and son were attacked with a sharp weapon at a hardware store in Kolonnawa in broad daylight. Separately, a woman was killed by a bus near Royal College, Colombo.

items.headline: Lightning warning for 17 districts
items.summary: The Met Department issued an amber lightning warning valid until 11:30 PM for 17 districts, including Colombo, Gampaha, Kandy and Jaffna, with thunderstorms likely this evening and tonight.

items.headline: Sri Lankans enter IPL 2027 auction
items.summary: Several Sri Lankan players have registered for the IPL 2027 auction; Newswire counts 21 while Daily Mirror reports seven.

items.headline: Colombia supermarket hostages freed
items.summary: Colombian security forces stormed a supermarket and freed all the hostages held by gunmen.

items.headline: China hits back after Huawei verdict
items.summary: China accused the US of suppressing Chinese companies after a US court convicted Huawei of fraud and trade-secret theft.

items.headline: Sri Lankan refugee dies in Eswatini
items.summary: A Sri Lankan refugee died months after being relocated by the UK to Eswatini.
